title: Gritty and Tired Eyes

patient.name: Mdm Koh Siew Eng
patient.presenting_complaint: Both eyes red and gritty, worse with screen use, no pain

history.hpc: Mdm Koh says 'My eyes feel gritty and red, like got sand inside, worse when I look at computer whole day. No pain, just tired and dry.' Both eyes, mild redness, burning/gritty feeling, no discharge, vision normal but fluctuates a bit.
history.pmhx: No serious eye problems. Long screen hours at work. Uses the air-con office all day.
history.social_hx: Office worker, long screen time, dry air-conditioned environment.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Mild bilateral redness, no discharge; surface dryness suspected (for doctor to confirm)

investigations.history_and_triage: Focused history shows a chronic, mild, gritty bilateral red eye with no pain, no discharge and normal vision, worse with screens and dry air — a dry-eye pattern rather than an acute infective or painful red eye.
investigations.red_flags_checked: No pain, no photophobia, no visual loss, no contact lens use — no sight-threatening red flags.
investigations.triage_category: Routine (Category 4) — minor/chronic; advise eye-care habits and routine review.

diagnosis: A mild, chronic, gritty bilateral red eye with no pain or discharge, worse with screen use and dry air, fits a dry-eye pattern. The PSA recognises there are no red flags, triages routinely, and advises simple measures. No medical diagnosis is made by the PSA.

immediate: Confirm identity and take a focused red-eye history including screen use and environment
Apply the red-eye differential and recognise the dry-eye pattern
Confirm there are no red flags (pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens use)
Record visual acuity and triage routinely
follow_up: Doctor to confirm and advise lubricants if needed
Advise return if pain, light sensitivity or reduced vision develop
patient_education: Explain screen breaks (look away regularly) and blinking often
Suggest reducing direct air-con/fan flow and using lubricant drops
Advise return if the eyes become painful or vision drops

key_points: Confirms identity and takes a focused red-eye history
Asks about screen use, environment and discharge
Asks about pain, photophobia and vision
Applies the red-eye differential and recognises the dry-eye pattern
Distinguishes it from an acute infective or painful red eye
Confirms there are no red flags
Notes screen use and dry environment as relevant
Recognises a likely minor (Category 4) chronic red eye
Does not make a medical diagnosis — routes routinely
Understands which features would raise the urgency
Links lifestyle factors to the symptoms
Advises return if red-flag symptoms develop
